topic: What Is Electronics - Signals, Components and Systems
title: What Is Electronics? Explained Simply | Engineering Electronics Ep 1
description:
Mahadev's ragi field dried out while he was away for three days, because nobody switched on the pump. Could a small circuit do the job for him? In this animated lesson we meet Project Neeru, four first-year engineering students in Mandya building a smart water controller for a farm, and use it to understand what electronics really is.

You will see the difference between electrical power (it does the work) and electronics (it uses current to carry information and make decisions), what a signal is, analog vs digital signals, passive vs active components, and the three jobs of every electronic system: sense, decide and act. Then we watch the controller run live for a whole day, with an oscilloscope tracing the soil sensor and the pump switching on and off by itself. We look at sense, decide and act at work today in a hospital monitor, a car airbag and a phone screen, and at the human side honestly: electronics saves water and lives, but it needs power, it can fail, and it creates e-waste. The UN Global E-waste Monitor 2024 reports 62 million tonnes of e-waste in 2022, with less than a quarter properly recycled.

This is Episode 1 of our Engineering Electronics series for ECE, E&TC and EEE students, year by year.
